definitions.explanation: A Shinto shrine enshrining {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす} as the deity {東照大権現|とうしょうだいごんげん}. The most famous is in {日光|にっこう}, a UNESCO World Heritage site, but Toshogu shrines exist throughout Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日光|にっこう}→日光：03515_nikkou⟧{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{祀|まつ}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。

{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{豪華|ごうか}→豪華：02815_gouka⟧な⟦{彫刻|ちょうこく}→彫刻：04448_choukoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{江戸時代|えどじだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{結晶|けっしょう}→結晶：13798_kesshou⟧だ。
examples.english: The lavish carvings of Toshogu Shrine are the crystallization of Edo-period craftsmanship.

notes:
Combination of {東照|とうしょう} (the posthumous title given to {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}) + {宮|ぐう} (shrine). Refers to any shrine dedicated to Ieyasu, of which there are over 100 across Japan.

WELL-KNOWN EXAMPLES:
- ⟦{日光|にっこう}→日光：03515_nikkou⟧{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}: Nikko Toshogu — the main and most famous shrine
- {久能山|くのうざん}{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}: Kunozan Toshogu — where Ieyasu was originally buried
- ⟦{上野|うえの}→上野：28394_ueno⟧{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}: Ueno Toshogu — in central Tokyo

CULTURAL NOTE:
Nikko Toshogu is famous for its elaborate gold-leaf decorations, the ⟦{三猿|さんざる}→三猿：28476_sanzaru⟧ (three wise monkeys) carving, and the {眠|ねむ}り{猫|ねこ} (sleeping cat) carving. It contrasts sharply with the simpler aesthetic typical of Shinto shrines.
